item.title: Rescue mission called off for NASA Swift space telescope, setting up a fiery reentry
item.summary: # Rescue mission called off for NASA Swift space telescope, setting up a fiery reentry - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - NASA and startup Katalyst Space Technologies call off a rescue of aging Swift space telescope after technical problems crippled the Link spacecraft, sealing Swift’s fate of fiery reentry later this year. - The $30-million mission aimed to raise Swift from a rapidly decaying orbit worsened by intense solar activity, preserving a telescope that spent two decades tracking cosmic explosions. - Although Swift will be lost, Katalyst plans to keep Link flying nearby as a test for future rescue efforts. CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — The mission to save NASA’s sinking Swift Observatory has been called off, dooming the telescope to a fiery reentry later this year. NASA and Katalyst Space Technologies announced the news last week, more than a month after the startup’s Link spacecraft rocketed away to the telescope’s rescue. Katalyst said Link will not attempt to capture Swift and boost it to a higher orbit because of problems with controlling the spacecraft.
